title: Breastfeeding and Formula Both Feed a Baby Well
hook: Health bodies recommend breastfeeding where possible, but properly prepared infant formula is a safe, nourishing alternative — a fed baby is the goal.
key_points: WHO and others recommend exclusive breastfeeding for about the first 6 months where feasible, then continued alongside solids.
Breast milk offers antibodies and adapts over time; it can also lower some infection risks for the baby.
Commercial infant formula is nutritionally complete and safe when prepared and stored as directed.
Feeding choices depend on health, circumstances, and support — and many families combine both.
content_html: The public-health message on infant feeding has two parts that sit comfortably together. First, where it's feasible, breastfeeding is recommended — the WHO advises exclusive breast milk for about the first six months, then breastfeeding alongside solids. Breast milk supplies antibodies, adapts to the baby over time, and can reduce some infection risks.
extra_html: Second, properly prepared commercial infant formula is a safe, nutritionally complete way to feed a baby, and following the preparation and storage instructions is what matters most for safety. Real feeding decisions hinge on health, circumstances, and the support a family has — and plenty of families combine breast and bottle. The honest summary is that a fed, thriving baby is the goal, and there's no need for guilt about how you get there. This is general information; a lactation consultant, midwife, or pediatrician can help with your specific situation.

related.title: Starting Solid Foods
related.hook: Most babies are ready for their first solid foods at around six months — alongside continued breast milk or formula, not instead of it.

related.title: Pumping and Storing Breast Milk
related.hook: Expressing milk lets someone else share feeds and keeps supply going when you're back at work. The trick is a simple storage rule — and gentle handling so the milk stays good for baby.

choices.text: Breast milk plus daily solid food from birth
Cow's milk as the main drink

flashcards.explanation_html: WHO recommends exclusive breastfeeding for about the first 6 months where possible, then continuing alongside appropriate solids.

flashcards.prompt: Is properly prepared infant formula a safe way to feed a baby?

choices.text: Yes — it's nutritionally complete when prepared and stored as directed
No — only breast milk can nourish a baby
Only if mixed with cow's milk

flashcards.explanation_html: Commercial infant formula is designed to be nutritionally complete. Safe preparation and storage matter; a fed baby is the goal.

flashcards.prompt: Name two things breast milk offers beyond basic nutrition.
flashcards.back_html: It provides antibodies, adapts over time to the baby, and can lower some infection risks — benefits formula doesn't fully replicate.
